newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Ammunition dump explosion rocks northwest Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Ammunition dump explosion rocks northwest Kabul.

text.p: A series of explosions rocked northwest Kabul on Tuesday morning when an ammunition dump caught fire in a military base.
The explosions in a Taleban military base in the Khair Khana district of Kabul started at 9 a.m. (0430 GMT) and lasted for more than an hour, witnesses said.
Smoke was still rising from the scene when journalists arrived, but Taleban guards at the base were denying access to the site.
Taleban fighters at the base said the fire had started by accident.

"An electrical fault started a fire in the wooden ceiling of a room where ammunition was stored. When the roof collapsed the ammunition started to explode," said one fighter who declined to give his name.
He discounted rumours that were circulating in the city on Tuesday morning that the fire had been started by sabotage or opposition rockets.
The base is on the road to the front line between the Taleban and the opposition alliance some 30 kilometres (19 miles) north of Kabul.
The purist Islamic Taleban have been facing opposition forces since October along a range of low hills that bisect the broad valley running north from Kabul into the foothills of the Hindu Kush.
